newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG prime minister Chan to step aside.
newsitem.headline: PNG prime minister Chan to step aside.

text.p: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan said on Wednesday he and two senior ministers would be stepping aside to allow a caretaker administration to take over before elections.
Chan told parliament that he, Deputy Prime Minister Chris Haiveta and Defence Minister Mathias Ijape would step aside.

"Mr Speaker, in the interest and for the good (of the nation) and in order to defuse something that I consider a little bit explosive outside, I will direct the deputy prime minister and the minister for defence to step aside," Chan said in an emotional speech to the assembly.

"I myself will step aside and I will have the cabinet to consider to appoint the acting prime minister," he said, adding that he would leave office for the duration of an inquiry into a controversial mercenary contract.

The news was greeted with a huge roar by thousands of protesters besieging the parliament building to demand Chan's departure over the mercenary contract. Elections are due in PNG in June and Chan said they could be brought forward.
